Dispersion / frequency bounds: Strong; deep water cᵍ=3cₚ/2
Propagation and speed: Shorter waves faster; energy at group speed
Typical source: Light wind, raindrops, interface disturbance
Main observations / relevance: High-frequency ripples, wave tanks

Medium / location: Free surface; motion decays with depth
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Deep water dispersive; cᵍ=cₚ/2
Propagation and speed: Longer deep-water waves faster; refract, shoal and break near shore
Typical source: Local wind, distant storms, vessels
Main observations / relevance: Buoy height/period, radar, altimetry

Dispersion / frequency bounds: Nearly non-dispersive at uniform depth; c=√(gH)
Propagation and speed: Fast in deep water, slows and grows near shore; basin crossing
Typical source: Seafloor earthquake, landslide, volcano, impact
Main observations / relevance: DART bottom pressure, tide gauges, GNSS buoys

Dispersion relation (K²=k²+l²): Forced frequency fixed; free modes locally ω²=f²+gHK²
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Nearly non-dispersive; resonance and friction shape response
Propagation and speed: Kelvin/Poincaré-like response in rotating basins
Typical source: Lunar and solar tidal potential
Main observations / relevance: Tide gauges, altimetry, current meters

Medium / location: Enclosed or semi-enclosed basins and harbours
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Discrete eigenmodes set by geometry
Propagation and speed: Fixed nodes/antinodes; persists under weak damping
Typical source: Wind setup, pressure jumps, tsunamis, ship waves
Main observations / relevance: Tide gauges, pressure sensors; harbour resonance risk

Restoring mechanism / balance: Wind stress and low pressure forcing; gravity adjustment
Dispersion relation (K²=k²+l²): No unique free dispersion; free part ≈f²+gHK²
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Controlled by topography, friction, resonance and storm motion
Propagation and speed: Adds to tides; amplified on shallow shelves and funnel bays
Typical source: Tropical/extratropical cyclones, persistent wind
Main observations / relevance: Gauges, buoys, pressure/wind fields and forecasts

Main approximation / vertical structure: Boussinesq, linear, uniform N and f
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Strongly dispersive; usually |f|<|ω|<N
Propagation and speed: Phase and energy directions differ; energy follows beams
Typical source: Tides over topography, wind, convection, shear
Main observations / relevance: T/S chains, ADCP, Argo/gliders, SAR

Main approximation / vertical structure: Internal-wave modes; ω fixed at tidal frequency
Dispersion relation (K²=k²+l²): ω=ωtide; horizontal wavenumber set by internal-wave dispersion and mode
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Multimodal, coherently basin-spanning; may steepen into solitary waves
Propagation and speed: Radiates from generation sites; modal group speeds differ
Typical source: Barotropic tide over ridges, straits and slopes
Main observations / relevance: Altimetry/SAR, moorings, profiles and microstructure

Medium / location: Ocean mixed layer and rotating-fluid interior
Main approximation / vertical structure: Free horizontal motion without pressure gradient
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Local frequency set by latitude; f→0 at equator
Propagation and speed: Horizontal velocity rotates clockwise in NH
Typical source: Abrupt wind change, mixed-layer adjustment
Main observations / relevance: Drifters, ADCP and current time series

Medium / location: Rotating shallow-water layer in ocean or atmosphere
Main approximation / vertical structure: f-plane, linear shallow water, speed c
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Cutoff at |f|; approaches gravity wave at high wavenumber
Propagation and speed: Propagates in any direction; phase and group speeds differ
Typical source: Rapid mass/momentum disturbance, geostrophic adjustment
Main observations / relevance: Sea level/geopotential and velocity spectra

Medium / location: Near a coast, slope or vertical boundary
Main approximation / vertical structure: Linear shallow water; zero normal flow at boundary
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Ideally non-dispersive; boundary selects one branch
Propagation and speed: In NH the coast lies to the right of propagation
Typical source: Wind, tides, tsunamis, boundary adjustment
Main observations / relevance: Coastal gauge phase and satellite altimetry

Restoring mechanism / balance: Background PV gradient β and PV conservation
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Strongly dispersive; phase usually westward in resting medium
Propagation and speed: Westward phase; group velocity can differ or be eastward
Typical source: Wind stress, heating, topography, flow instability
Main observations / relevance: SSH/geopotential, OLR, reanalysis and Hovmöller diagrams

Restoring mechanism / balance: Topographic PV gradient from depth changes
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Low-frequency dispersive; sign depends on coordinates/slope
Propagation and speed: Along isobaths; often shallow water on right in NH
Typical source: Slope-current disturbances, wind, eddies and tides
Main observations / relevance: Shelf current arrays, bottom pressure and sea level

Restoring mechanism / balance: Gravity plus β effect; meridional velocity v=0
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Ideally non-dispersive; Gaussian meridional trapping
Propagation and speed: Eastward; first oceanic baroclinic mode often 2–3 m s⁻¹
Typical source: Wind anomalies, MJO/convection, ENSO adjustment
Main observations / relevance: Equatorial SSH, thermocline depth, OLR and wind

Dispersion / frequency bounds: Dispersive; westward in resting medium
Propagation and speed: Westward; gyre pairs straddle equator
Typical source: Tropical heating, wind stress and reflected Kelvin waves
Main observations / relevance: OLR, winds, SSH and thermocline anomalies

Dispersion / frequency bounds: Westward long waves are Rossby-like; eastward short waves gravity-like
Propagation and speed: Eastward or westward; meridional wind antisymmetric
Typical source: Tropical convection, wind and initial disturbances
Main observations / relevance: OLR–wind spectra, equatorial currents/SSH

Dispersion / frequency bounds: Eastward and westward high-frequency branches; trapped
Propagation and speed: Faster phase than equatorial Rossby; energy may propagate vertically
Typical source: Deep convection, heating pulses, geostrophic adjustment
Main observations / relevance: OLR, winds, temperature and geopotential spectra

Medium / location: Stably stratified troposphere to upper atmosphere
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Strongly dispersive; mountain waves often ω≈0 in ground frame
Propagation and speed: Energy often upward; breaking produces gravity-wave drag
Typical source: Topography, convection, jets/fronts and shear
Main observations / relevance: Satellite brightness/airglow, radar, soundings, lidar

Medium / location: Compressible ocean or atmosphere; most familiar in air
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Non-dispersive in ideal uniform medium; speed cₛ
Propagation and speed: Longitudinal compression wave; ~340 m s⁻¹ in air, ~1500 m s⁻¹ in seawater
Typical source: Explosions, thunderstorms, volcanoes, mechanical vibration
Main observations / relevance: Microbarometers, hydrophones, acoustic remote sensing

Main approximation / vertical structure: Isothermal/hydrostatic atmosphere; near-zero vertical velocity, evanescent
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Nearly non-dispersive ideally; can circle the globe repeatedly
Propagation and speed: Near-acoustic horizontal speed; strong surface-pressure signal
Typical source: Major eruptions, explosions and intense convection
Main observations / relevance: Global infrasound and surface-pressure networks

Medium / location: Global atmosphere; amplitude often increases with height
Restoring mechanism / balance: Periodic solar heating/tidal potential; gravity and rotation
Main approximation / vertical structure: Laplace tidal equations; Hough horizontal modes
Dispersion relation (K²=k²+l²): Forced at 24 h, 12 h, etc.; vertical wavenumber set by equivalent depth
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Multiple Hough modes; affected by radiation, friction and mean wind
Propagation and speed: Migrating tide follows the Sun westward; nonmigrating tides vary
Typical source: Solar absorption by ozone/water vapour, latent heating and topography
Main observations / relevance: Radar, satellite temperature/winds and pressure

Medium / location: Midlatitude tropospheric jets and frontal zones
Restoring mechanism / balance: PV gradients; baroclinic instability can amplify disturbances
Dispersion relation (K²=k²+l²): Real part Rossby-like: ω≈Uk−βk/(K²+Rd⁻²); Im(ω)>0 when unstable
Dispersion / frequency bounds: Propagating and growing; not a purely neutral free wave
Propagation and speed: Usually eastward with westerlies; group velocity drives downstream development
Typical source: Available potential energy from meridional temperature gradient and vertical shear
Main observations / relevance: 500-hPa height, satellite clouds and reanalysis vorticity/PV
